title: Grammaire - Present Simple et Present Continuous et Present Simple vs Present Continuous
content:
## Formation et emploi

Le Present Simple exprime les habitudes, les vérités générales et les états permanents. Formation : sujet + base verbale (+ s à la 3e personne du singulier). I/You/We/They work. He/She/It works. Négation : sujet + do/does + not + base verbale. He does not (doesn't) work. Question : Do/Does + sujet + base verbale? Does he work? Marqueurs de temps : always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day/week.

## Formation et emploi

Le Present Continuous (ou Progressive) exprime une action en cours au moment où l'on parle. Formation : sujet + BE (am/is/are) + verbe-ING. I am working. She is reading. They are playing. Négation : sujet + BE + not + verbe-ING. He is not (isn't) working. Question : BE + sujet + verbe-ING? Are you listening? Marqueurs : now, at the moment, right now, currently. Attention : certains verbes d'état ne s'emploient pas au continuous (like, want, know, believe).

## Present Simple vs Present Continuous

Present Simple : habitudes, routines, vérités générales. 'I play football every Saturday' (habitude). 'Water boils at 100°C' (vérité). Present Continuous : action en cours maintenant. 'I am playing football right now' (en ce moment). Comparaison : 'She works in a bank' (son métier, permanent) vs 'She is working at home today' (exceptionnellement, temporaire). Le choix dépend si l'action est habituelle/permanente (Simple) ou temporaire/en cours (Continuous).

title: Grammaire - Past Simple et Past Simple (Preterit)
content:
## Verbes irréguliers courants

Les verbes irréguliers ont une forme passée spécifique à mémoriser. Essentiels : be → was/were, have → had, do → did, go → went, come → came, see → saw, make → made, take → took, get → got, give → gave, know → knew, think → thought, say → said, tell → told, find → found, leave → left, feel → felt, become → became, begin → began, write → wrote, read → read, eat → ate, drink → drank, run → ran, speak → spoke. La forme est la même à toutes les personnes.

## Verbes réguliers

Le Past Simple (Preterit) exprime une action passée, terminée, datée. Verbes réguliers : base verbale + ED. I worked, she played, they watched. Règles d'orthographe : verbe en -e → + d (lived), consonne + y → ied (studied), consonne finale doublée si syllabe accentuée (stopped). Négation : sujet + did not (didn't) + base verbale. She didn't work. Question : Did + sujet + base verbale? Did you work? Marqueurs : yesterday, last week/month/year, ago, in 2020.

title: Present Perfect - Introduction
content: Le Present Perfect relie le passé au présent. Il exprime une expérience de vie ou une action passée avec un résultat présent. Formation : sujet + have/has + participe passé. I have visited Paris. She has finished her homework. Négation : haven't/hasn't + participe passé. Question : Have/Has + sujet + participe passé? Have you ever been to London? Marqueurs : ever (déjà, questions), never (jamais), already (déjà, affirm.), yet (pas encore), just (juste), since/for (depuis).

title: Grammaire - Future avec Will et Future avec Going to
content:
## Future avec Will

Will exprime le futur pour des prédictions, des décisions spontanées ou des promesses. Formation : sujet + will + base verbale. I will help you. It will rain tomorrow. Forme contractée : I'll, you'll, he'll... Négation : will not (won't) + base verbale. I won't forget. Question : Will + sujet + base verbale? Will you come? Emplois : prédiction ('It will be sunny'), décision immédiate ('I'll answer the phone'), promesse ('I will always love you'), offre ('I'll carry your bag').

## Future avec Going to

Going to exprime une intention ou une prédiction basée sur des indices présents. Formation : sujet + BE (am/is/are) + going to + base verbale. I am going to study medicine. Négation : BE + not + going to. She isn't going to come. Question : BE + sujet + going to? Are you going to travel? Emplois : intention planifiée ('I'm going to visit my grandma this weekend'), prédiction avec indices ('Look at those clouds, it's going to rain'). Will = spontané/général, Going to = planifié/indices.

title: Grammaire - Modal CAN et Modal MUST et Modal SHOULD
content:
## Capacité et permission

CAN exprime la capacité (savoir faire) ou la permission. Formation : sujet + can + base verbale (sans to). I can swim. She can speak French. Négation : cannot (can't). I can't drive. Question : Can + sujet + base verbale? Can you help me? Emplois : capacité ('He can play the guitar'), permission informelle ('You can use my phone'), possibilité ('It can be cold in winter'). Passé : could. 'I could swim when I was 5.' Could est aussi plus poli pour les demandes : 'Could you help me, please?'

## Obligation et déduction

MUST exprime une obligation forte ou une déduction logique. Formation : sujet + must + base verbale. You must wear a seatbelt. Négation : must not (mustn't) = interdiction. You mustn't smoke here. Question : Must + sujet + base verbale? (rare). Emplois : obligation ('You must do your homework'), interdiction ('You mustn't be late'), déduction ('He must be tired, he worked all day'). Alternative pour obligation : have to (plus courant). 'I have to go now.'

## Conseil

SHOULD exprime un conseil, une recommandation ou ce qui serait bien de faire. Formation : sujet + should + base verbale. You should eat more vegetables. Négation : should not (shouldn't). You shouldn't stay up late. Question : Should + sujet + base verbale? Should I call him? Emplois : conseil ('You should see a doctor'), reproche ('You should have called me'), opinion ('I think we should leave now'). Should est moins fort que must : c'est un conseil, pas une obligation.

title: Les pronoms personnels sujets et compléments
content: Pronoms sujets (avant le verbe) : I (je), you (tu/vous), he (il), she (elle), it (il/elle neutre), we (nous), they (ils/elles). Pronoms compléments (après le verbe ou préposition) : me (me/moi), you (te/toi/vous), him (le/lui), her (la/lui), it (le/la/lui), us (nous), them (les/leur). Exemples : 'I love her' (je l'aime), 'She loves me' (elle m'aime), 'Give it to them' (donne-le-leur). Le pronom complément suit toujours le verbe ou la préposition.

title: Les adjectifs possessifs
content: Les adjectifs possessifs précèdent le nom et indiquent la possession. My (mon/ma/mes), your (ton/ta/tes, votre/vos), his (son/sa/ses - possesseur masculin), her (son/sa/ses - possesseur féminin), its (son/sa/ses - neutre), our (notre/nos), their (leur/leurs). En anglais, l'adjectif possessif s'accorde avec le possesseur, pas avec l'objet possédé. 'His mother' (sa mère, à lui), 'Her father' (son père, à elle). 'Their books' (leurs livres).

title: There is / There are - Existence
content: There is/are exprime l'existence ou la présence de quelque chose. There is + singulier/indénombrable : 'There is a book on the table.' 'There is some milk.' There are + pluriel : 'There are three cats in the garden.' Négation : There isn't / There aren't. 'There isn't any water.' Question : Is there / Are there? 'Is there a bank near here?' 'Are there any questions?' Passé : There was (singulier), There were (pluriel).

title: Vocabulaire - L'école et la vie quotidienne
content: L'école : school, classroom, teacher, student/pupil, headteacher (principal), lesson, subject, homework, exam/test, break (récréation), canteen (cantine). Matières : English, French, maths, science, history, geography, PE (physical education), art, music. Objets : book, notebook, pen, pencil, ruler, rubber (gomme), schoolbag, desk, board. Actions : to study, to learn, to teach, to read, to write, to listen, to understand, to pass (réussir), to fail (échouer).

title: Vocabulaire - Les loisirs et activités
content: Sports : football, basketball, tennis, swimming, running, cycling, skiing, skating. Loisirs : reading, watching TV, playing video games, listening to music, cooking, drawing, photography. Musique : to play the guitar/piano/drums, to sing, band, concert. Sortir : to go to the cinema/movies, to go shopping, to hang out with friends. Fréquence : I often play... I sometimes go... I never watch... Expression des goûts : I like/love/enjoy + verbe-ING. I don't like/hate + verbe-ING.

title: Vocabulaire - La famille et les relations
content: Famille proche : mother/mum, father/dad, parents, brother, sister, son, daughter, children. Famille élargie : grandfather/grandpa, grandmother/grandma, grandparents, uncle, aunt, cousin, nephew, niece. Relations : friend, best friend, boyfriend, girlfriend, neighbour. Descriptions : single child (enfant unique), twins (jumeaux), stepmother/stepfather (belle-mère/beau-père), half-brother/sister (demi-frère/sœur). Expressions : 'I have two brothers', 'She is an only child', 'We are a big family'.

title: Poser des questions - Mots interrogatifs
content: Mots interrogatifs (WH-questions) : What (quoi, quel), Who (qui), Where (où), When (quand), Why (pourquoi), How (comment). Structure : WH-word + auxiliaire + sujet + verbe? 'What do you want?' 'Where does she live?' 'Why are you late?' How + adjectif : How old (quel âge), How much/many (combien), How often (à quelle fréquence), How long (combien de temps), How far (à quelle distance). Yes/No questions : auxiliaire en premier. 'Do you like pizza?' 'Is she French?'
